script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we explore a phrase that captures the essence of non-stop talking. [break 1s] The phrase is: 喋喋不休, dié dié bù xiū. [break 1s] 喋 (dié) — to chatter; [break 0.5s] 喋 (dié) — to chatter; [break 0.5s] 不 (bù) — not; [break 0.5s] 休 (xiū) — to stop. [break 1s] The full idiom is 喋喋不休, which literally means 'to chatter non-stop' and figuratively refers to someone who talks endlessly. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] The idiom originated from ancient Chinese literature where it described people who had nothing significant to say but continued to talk. Their incessant chatter was often seen as annoying or unnecessary. Over time, it became a common expression to describe those who just wouldn't stop talking. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 他总是喋喋不休，没完没了。 [break 1s] He is always chattering endlessly, never stopping. [break 1s] Example 2: 在会议上，有些人喋喋不休，浪费了时间。 [break 1s] In the meeting, some people talked non-stop, wasting time. [break 1s] Example 3: 她的喋喋不休让我感到很疲惫。 [break 1s] Her endless chatter makes me feel very tired. [break 1s] So, we have 喋喋不休, which means endlessly chattering. Thank you for listening, and see you next time for another idiom! [break 1s]
